chapters.title: 1. Environment, Ecology & Biodiversity Basics
chapters.notes:
### 1.1 Environment and its parts
Environment = all living (biotic) and non-living (abiotic) things around an organism. The EP Act 1986 defines it as water, air and land and their inter-relationship with human beings, other living creatures, plants, micro-organisms and property.
| Sphere | What it is |
|---|---|
| Atmosphere | Air layer: N₂ about 78%, O₂ about 21%, Ar about 0.93%, CO₂ about 0.04% (above 420 ppm now) |
| Hydrosphere | All water. About 97.5% is salt water; only about 2.5% is fresh, and most of that is ice |
| Lithosphere | Rocks and soil |
| Biosphere | Zone where life exists, where the other three meet |
| Layers of the atmosphere (bottom to top) |  |

| Troposphere (weather, 8–18 km) | ➜ Stratosphere (ozone layer, 15–35 km) ➜ |
|---|---|

| Mesosphere (coldest) | ➜ Thermosphere / Ionosphere (radio waves) ➜ Exosphere |
|---|---|

### 1.2 Ecology and ecosystems
- Ecology: study of relations between organisms and their environment. The term was coined by Ernst Haeckel (1866). Ecosystem: term by A.G. Tansley (1935).
- Parts: abiotic (sun, water, soil, minerals) and biotic – producers (green plants), consumers (herbivores = primary, carnivores = secondary/tertiary), decomposers (bacteria, fungi).
- Food chain: grass ➜ grasshopper ➜ frog ➜ snake ➜ eagle. Food web = many linked chains (more stable).
- 10% law (Lindeman, 1942): only about 10% of energy passes from one trophic level to the next;
- the rest is lost as heat. So food chains are short (4–5 levels).
- Ecological pyramids: of number, biomass and energy. The pyramid of energy is always upright.
- The pyramid of biomass in a pond is inverted.
- Energy flow is one-way; nutrients cycle (carbon, nitrogen, water, phosphorus cycles).
- Ecological succession: gradual change of a community, ending in a stable climax community.
- Pioneer species on bare rock: lichens.
- Ecotone: transition zone between two ecosystems (e.g. mangroves between land and sea). Edge effect: more species at the ecotone.
### 1.3 Biodiversity
- Term popularised by E.O. Wilson (1988). Three levels: genetic, species and ecosystem diversity.
- India has about 2.4% of the world's land but about 7–8% of recorded species. India is one of 17 megadiverse countries.
- Biodiversity hotspots (Norman Myers, 1988): world has 36. India has parts of 4: Himalaya, Indo- Burma (North-East), Western Ghats & Sri Lanka, Sundaland (Nicobar Islands).
- Threats ("HIPPO"): Habitat loss, Invasive species (water hyacinth, Lantana, Parthenium), Pollution, Population, Over-exploitation; plus climate change.
- Conservation: in-situ (in natural home – national parks, sanctuaries, biosphere reserves, sacred groves) and ex-situ (outside – zoos, botanical gardens, seed and gene banks, e.g. Svalbard Global Seed Vault).
- IUCN Red List categories: Extinct, Extinct in the Wild, Critically Endangered, Endangered, Vulnerable, Near Threatened, Least Concern. IUCN founded 1948, HQ Gland, Switzerland.
| Law / treaty | Year & fact |
|---|---|
| Wildlife (Protection) Act | 1972; schedules of protected species (rationalised to 4 schedules by the 2022 amendment) |
| Forest (Conservation) Act | 1980; renamed Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam by the 2023 amendment |
| Biological Diversity Act | 2002; National Biodiversity Authority (Chennai), State Biodiversity Boards, Biodiversity Management Committees and People's Biodiversity Registers |
| Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) | Rio 1992. Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (Dec 2022): "30 by 30" – protect 30% of land and sea by 2030 |
| Ramsar Convention | 1971, Ramsar (Iran), on wetlands. World Wetlands Day 2 February |
| CITES | 1973, controls trade in endangered species |
| Project Tiger · Project Elephant | 1973 · 1992 |

### 1.4 West Bengal – environment facts
| Place | Fact |
|---|---|
| Sundarbans | World's largest mangrove forest (shared with Bangladesh). Tiger Reserve 1973, National Park 1984, UNESCO World Heritage 1987, Biosphere Reserve 1989, Ramsar site 2019 (India's largest Ramsar site). Home of the Royal Bengal Tiger. Name from the Sundari tree (Heritiera fomes) |
| East Kolkata Wetlands | Ramsar site 2002; natural sewage treatment through fish ponds |
| National parks | Sundarban, Buxa (also tiger reserve), Jaldapara (one-horned rhino), Gorumara (rhino), Neora Valley, Singalila (red panda) |
| Hotspot | North Bengal hills fall in the Himalaya hotspot |
| State symbols | Animal – fishing cat; bird – white-throated kingfisher; tree – chhatim; flower – shiuli (night jasmine) |

### 1.5 Important environment days

| 3 Mar | World Wildlife Day |

| 8 Jun · 29 Jul | Oceans Day · Tiger Day |

| 2 Dec · 14 Dec | Pollution Control Day · Energy Conservation Day |

## বাংলা নোট – অধ্যায় ১: পরিবেশ ও জীববৈচিত্র্য
- বায়ুমণ্ডলে নাইট্রোজেন ~৭৮%, অক্সিজেন ~২১%, CO₂ ~০.০৪%। ওজোন স্তর থাকে স্ট্র্যাটোস্ফিয়ারে; আবহাওয়া ট্রপোস্ফিয়ারে।
- "ইকোলজি" শব্দ হেকেল (১৮৬৬), "ইকোসিস্টেম" ট্যান্সলি (১৯৩৫)। উৎপাদক ➜ খাদক ➜ বিয়োজক।
- ১০% সূত্র (লিন্ডেম্যান): এক খাদ্যস্তর থেকে পরেরটিতে মাত্র ~১০% শক্তি যায়। শক্তির পিরামিড সবসময় সোজা।
- শক্তিপ্রবাহ একমুখী, পুষ্টি চক্রাকারে ঘোরে।
- জীববৈচিত্র্যের তিন স্তর: জিনগত, প্রজাতিগত, বাস্তুতন্ত্রগত। ভারত ১৭টি মেগাডাইভার্স দেশের একটি। বিশ্বে ৩৬টি হটস্পট, ভারতে ৪টি: হিমালয়, ইন্দো-বার্মা, পশ্চিমঘাট, সুন্দাল্যান্ড।
- সংরক্ষণ: ইন-সিটু (জাতীয় উদ্যান, অভয়ারণ্য) ও এক্স-সিটু (চিড়িয়াখানা, বীজ ব্যাংক)।
- আইন: বন্যপ্রাণী সুরক্ষা আইন ১৯৭২, বন সংরক্ষণ আইন ১৯৮০, জীববৈচিত্র্য আইন ২০০২। রামসার কনভেনশন ১৯৭১; কুনমিং-মন্ট্রিয়ল কাঠামো (২০২২) — "৩০ বাই ৩০"।
- সুন্দরবন: বিশ্বের বৃহত্তম ম্যানগ্রোভ; UNESCO ১৯৮৭, রামসার ২০১৯; রয়্যাল বেঙ্গল টাইগার; নাম সুন্দরী গাছ থেকে।
- পূর্ব কলকাতা জলাভূমি রামসার ২০০২।
- জাতীয় উদ্যান: বক্সা, জলদাপাড়া (গণ্ডার), গরুমারা, নেওড়া ভ্যালি, সিঙ্গালিলা (রেড পান্ডা)। রাজ্য প্রাণী — বাঘরোল (ফিশিং ক্যাট)।
- দিবস: বিশ্ব পরিবেশ দিবস ৫ জুন, ওজোন দিবস ১৬ সেপ্টেম্বর, জাতীয় শক্তি সংরক্ষণ দিবস ১৪ ডিসেম্বর।

chapters.title: 2. Major Environmental Issues
chapters.notes:
### 2.1 Air pollution
- Primary pollutants are emitted directly: SO₂, NOx, CO, particulate matter (PM), hydrocarbons, lead.
- Secondary pollutants form in the air: ground-level ozone (O₃), PAN (peroxyacetyl nitrate), sulphuric and nitric acid, secondary PM.
- PM₂.₅ (below 2.5 µm) goes deep into the lungs and blood; it is the most harmful common pollutant. PM₁₀ = below 10 µm.
- Carbon monoxide binds haemoglobin about 200–250 times more strongly than oxygen.
- Indoor pollution: smoke from chulhas (biomass cooking) ➜ PM Ujjwala Yojana (2016) gave LPG to poor households.
| Classical (London) smog | Photochemical (Los Angeles) smog |
|---|---|
| Smoke + fog + SO₂; cold, humid weather; reducing in nature | NOx + hydrocarbons + sunlight ➜ O₃, PAN; warm, sunny; oxidising in nature |
| Great London Smog, Dec 1952 (about 4,000+ deaths) | Eye irritation, breathing problems; common in big cities |

Temperature inversion (warm air above cold air) traps pollutants near the ground, especially on winter nights.
### 2.2 Acid rain
- Rain with pH below 5.6. (Normal rain is slightly acidic, about 5.6, because of CO₂ forming carbonic acid.)
- Caused by SO₂ and NOx from coal power plants, smelters and vehicles ➜ H₂SO₄ and HNO₃.
- Effects: harms lakes, fish, forests, soil; corrodes buildings – "stone cancer" of the Taj Mahal (Mathura refinery issue; Taj Trapezium Zone, SC 1996).
- Control: FGD, low-sulphur coal, catalytic converters, liming of lakes.
### 2.3 Ozone layer depletion
- The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs harmful UV-B rays. Measured in Dobson Units (DU);
- a value below 220 DU is called an "ozone hole".
- Main culprits: CFCs (chlorofluorocarbons – refrigerants, aerosols), halons, carbon tetrachloride, methyl bromide. One chlorine atom can destroy about 1 lakh ozone molecules.
- The Antarctic ozone hole was reported by Farman, Gardiner and Shanklin in 1985. It forms in the southern spring (Sep–Oct) due to polar stratospheric clouds.
- Effects of more UV: skin cancer, cataract, weaker immunity, harm to plankton and crops.
- Ozone treaties Vienna Convention 1985 ➜ Montreal Protocol 1987 (16 Sep; phase out ozone-depleting substances; the most successful environmental treaty, the only UN treaty ratified by all countries) ➜ Kigali Amendment 2016 (phase down HFCs, which are greenhouse gases). India ratified Kigali in 2021; India's HFC freeze is 2028.
### 2.4 Water pollution
- Sources: sewage (biggest), industrial effluents, agricultural run-off (fertilisers, pesticides), oil spills, thermal discharge.
- Eutrophication: extra nitrates and phosphates ➜ algal bloom ➜ low dissolved oxygen ➜ fish die.
- Water hyacinth spreads ("terror of Bengal").
- Biomagnification: concentration of non-degradable toxins (DDT, mercury) increases up the food chain. Bioaccumulation: build-up inside one organism.
- Groundwater arsenic: West Bengal is one of the worst-affected states (Murshidabad, Malda, Nadia, North and South 24 Parganas, Bardhaman). Causes arsenicosis (skin lesions, cancer).
- Fluoride in Purulia, Bankura, Birbhum causes fluorosis.
- Indicators: BOD, COD, DO, coliform count (sewage). Clean drinking water BOD < 1–2 mg/l.
- Missions: Namami Gange (2014), Jal Jeevan Mission (2019, tap water to every rural home), AMRUT.
### 2.5 Soil pollution, land degradation and desertification
- Causes: excess chemical fertilisers and pesticides, industrial waste dumping, mining, plastics, salinity from over-irrigation, soil erosion.
- About one-third of India's land faces degradation or desertification (ISRO Desertification Atlas).
- India's target: restore 26 million hectares of degraded land by 2030.
- UNCCD (1994) is the treaty on desertification. Desertification & Drought Day: 17 June.
### 2.6 Solid waste, plastic and e-waste
- India makes about 1.5–1.6 lakh tonnes of municipal solid waste a day (approx.). Swachh Bharat Mission started 2 Oct 2014.
- Plastic: identified single-use plastics banned from 1 July 2022. Microplastics (below 5 mm) are found in water, soil, food and even human blood.
- E-waste: India is the 3rd largest generator after China and USA. It contains lead, mercury, cadmium, brominated flame retardants. Rules: E-Waste (Management) Rules 2022 with EPR.
- Fly ash from coal power plants: used in cement, bricks and road building; 100% use is required by notification.
### 2.7 Other issues
| Issue | Key points |
|---|---|
| Noise pollution | Measured in dB; hearing loss, stress, high BP. Noise Rules 2000 |
| Thermal pollution | Hot water from power plants lowers oxygen in rivers |
| Radioactive pollution | Nuclear waste, accidents (Chernobyl 1986, Fukushima 2011) |
| Deforestation | India State of Forest Report (ISFR, by FSI Dehradun, every 2 years): forest + tree cover about 25% of area; target 33% (National Forest Policy 1988) |
| Mining | Land subsidence and mine fires (Raniganj, Jharia), dust, water pollution |
| Coastal issues in WB | Sea-level rise and erosion in the Sundarbans; disappearing islands (Lohachara, Ghoramara); cyclones Aila (2009), Amphan (May 2020), Yaas (2021), Remal (2024) |
| Urban heat island | Cities warmer than surroundings due to concrete and less greenery |

## বাংলা নোট – অধ্যায় ২: প্রধান পরিবেশগত সমস্যা
- প্রাথমিক দূষক সরাসরি নির্গত হয় (SO₂, NOx, CO); গৌণ দূষক বাতাসে তৈরি হয় (ভূপৃষ্ঠের ওজোন, PAN)। PM₂.₅ সবচেয়ে ক্ষতিকর।
- লন্ডন স্মগ (১৯৫২): ধোঁয়া + কুয়াশা + SO₂, বিজারক। ফটোকেমিক্যাল স্মগ: NOx + হাইড্রোকার্বন + সূর্যালোক, জারক। তাপমাত্রার বৈপরীত্য দূষণ আটকে রাখে।
- অম্লবৃষ্টি: pH ৫.৬-এর কম; কারণ SO₂ ও NOx। তাজমহলের "স্টোন ক্যানসার"।
- ওজোন ক্ষয়: CFC প্রধান দায়ী; ডবসন ইউনিটে মাপা; অ্যান্টার্কটিকায় ওজোন গহ্বর (১৯৮৫)। ভিয়েনা কনভেনশন ১৯৮৫, মন্ট্রিয়ল প্রোটোকল ১৯৮৭, কিগালি সংশোধনী ২০১৬ (HFC হ্রাস)।
- ইউট্রোফিকেশন: নাইট্রেট-ফসফেট বাড়লে শৈবাল বৃদ্ধি, অক্সিজেন কমে মাছ মরে। বায়োম্যাগনিফিকেশন:
- খাদ্যশৃঙ্খলে উপরে উঠলে DDT, পারদের ঘনত্ব বাড়ে।
- রাজ্যে ভূগর্ভস্থ জলে আর্সেনিক (মুর্শিদাবাদ, মালদহ, নদিয়া, ২৪ পরগনা) ও ফ্লোরাইড (পুরুলিয়া, বাঁকুড়া, বীরভূম)।
- কঠিন বর্জ্য: স্বচ্ছ ভারত মিশন (২ অক্টোবর ২০১৪); একবার-ব্যবহার্য প্লাস্টিক নিষিদ্ধ ১ জুলাই ২০২২; ই-বর্জ্যে ভারত তৃতীয়।
- বনভূমি + বৃক্ষ আচ্ছাদন প্রায় ২৫%; লক্ষ্য ৩৩%। সুন্দরবনে সমুদ্রতল বৃদ্ধি, লোহাচড়া দ্বীপ বিলুপ্ত; ঘূর্ণিঝড় আইলা (২০০৯), আমফান (২০২০)।

chapters.title: 3. Climate Change: Science, Treaties & India's Commitments

### 3.1 Greenhouse effect and global warming
- Greenhouse effect: gases in the air let sunlight in but trap outgoing heat (infra-red). Without it Earth would be about −18 °C instead of about +15 °C. The extra effect caused by humans = global warming.
- Earth is now about 1.2–1.3 °C warmer than pre-industrial times (1850–1900). Atmospheric CO₂ has risen from about 280 ppm to above 420 ppm (Mauna Loa record, Keeling Curve).
| Gas | Main sources | Global Warming Potential (100 yr, approx.) |
|---|---|---|
| Carbon dioxide (CO₂) | Burning fossil fuels, deforestation, cement | 1 (reference) |
| Methane (CH₄) | Paddy fields, cattle, landfills, coal mines, gas leaks | about 28 |
| Nitrous oxide (N₂O) | Nitrogen fertilisers | about 265 |
| HFCs, PFCs | Refrigerants, aluminium smelting | Hundreds to thousands |
| Sulphur hexafluoride (SF₆) | Electrical switchgear | about 23,500 (highest) |
| Water vapour | Natural | Biggest natural greenhouse gas |

Kyoto Protocol basket: CO₂, CH₄, N₂O, HFCs, PFCs, SF₆ (+ NF₃ added later). CO₂ contributes the most warming overall because of its huge volume.
Effects of climate change Melting glaciers and ice sheets, sea-level rise, more heat waves, floods, droughts and stronger cyclones, coral bleaching, ocean acidification, falling crop yields, spread of diseases (malaria, dengue), climate migration. The Sundarbans and coastal West Bengal are highly vulnerable.
- Mitigation = reduce emissions or increase sinks (renewables, efficiency, forests). Adaptation = adjust to impacts (embankments, drought-resistant crops, early warning).
- Carbon sink: forests, oceans, soil. Carbon footprint: total GHG emitted by a person, product or firm. Net zero: emissions balanced by removals.
- Carbon credit: 1 credit = 1 tonne of CO₂-equivalent reduced or removed.
### 3.2 Milestones of international action

|---|---|---|

| 1988 | IPCC set up by WMO and UNEP | Assessment reports; AR6 synthesis 2023; Nobel Peace Prize 2007 |

No fossil-fuel phase-out in the main text |

- Principle to remember CBDR-RC – Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (Rio 1992).
- Developed countries polluted more historically, so they should do more and give finance and technology. India strongly supports it.
### 3.3 India's climate commitments
Panchamrit (COP26, Glasgow, 2021)
1. 500 GW non-fossil electricity capacity by 2030.
2. 50% of energy requirement from renewables by 2030.
3. Cut projected carbon emissions by 1 billion tonnes by 2030.
4. Cut the emissions intensity of GDP by 45% (from 2005 levels) by 2030.
5. Net zero by 2070.
Updated NDC (August 2022)
- Emissions intensity of GDP down 45% by 2030 from 2005 level.
- About 50% of installed power capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030. Achieved in June 2025, five years early (PIB).
- Extra carbon sink of 2.5–3 billion tonnes CO₂e through forests and tree cover by 2030.
- Promote a healthy, sustainable lifestyle – Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment, launched Oct 2022).
National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC, 2008) – 8 missions
| # | Mission |
|---|---|
| 1 | National Solar Mission (JNNSM, 2010) |
| 2 | National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency (NMEEE – PAT, MTEE, EEFP, FEEED) |
| 3 | Sustainable Habitat |
| 4 | National Water Mission |
| 5 | Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem |
| 6 | Green India Mission |
| 7 | Sustainable Agriculture |
| 8 | Strategic Knowledge for Climate Change |

States have their own plans: the West Bengal State Action Plan on Climate Change (SAPCC).
**Market and other tools**
- Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), 2023: India's own carbon market under the Energy Conservation Act (amended 2022). BEE is the administrator; emission-intensity targets for sectors like aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali, pulp & paper.
- Green Credit Programme (Oct 2023): credits for tree planting, water saving and other green actions.
- International Solar Alliance (ISA): launched at COP21 (2015) by India and France; HQ Gurugram; "One Sun One World One Grid".

chapters.title: 4. Energy Resources & India's Energy Scenario
chapters.notes:
### 4.1 Classification of energy sources
| Basis | Type A | Type B |
|---|---|---|
| Can it be replaced? | Renewable: solar, wind, hydro, biomass, geothermal, tidal | Non-renewable: coal, oil, natural gas, uranium |
| Use history | Conventional: coal, oil, gas, large hydro, firewood | Non-conventional: solar, wind, tidal, geothermal, hydrogen |
| Form | Primary: found in nature (coal, crude oil, sunlight) | Secondary: made from primary (electricity, petrol, hydrogen) |
| Trade | Commercial: coal, oil, electricity | Non-commercial: firewood, cow dung, crop waste |

### 4.2 Energy units and conversions
- Must-know conversions
- Energy = Power × Time. Power in watt (W); energy in joule (J) or kWh.
- 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ ≈ 860 kcal (1 "unit" of electricity)
- 1 calorie = 4.186 J · 1 BTU ≈ 1,055 J · 1 HP = 746 W
- 1 toe (tonne of oil equivalent) ≈ 10⁷ kcal ≈ 41.87 GJ
- 1 MW = 1,000 kW; 1 GW = 1,000 MW
- Hydrogen has the highest energy per kg of any fuel (about 120–142 MJ/kg).
- Capacity factor / Plant Load Factor (PLF) = actual output ÷ maximum possible output. Coal plants run at about 65–75%, solar about 18–25%, wind about 25–35%.
- Energy intensity = energy used per unit of GDP (lower is better). Energy security = reliable, affordable supply.
### 4.3 India's power capacity (latest)
| Source | Installed capacity as on 31 Mar 2026 (PIB) |
|---|---|
| Solar | 150.26 GW |
| Wind | 56.09 GW |
| Large hydro | 51.41 GW |
| Bio-energy | 11.75 GW |
| Small hydro (up to 25 MW) | 5.17 GW |
| Total renewable (incl. large hydro) | 274.68 GW |
| Nuclear | 8.78 GW |
| Total non-fossil | 283.46 GW |

- Record 55.3 GW of non-fossil capacity was added in FY 2025-26.
- Reports say India crossed 300 GW non-fossil capacity by 31 July 2026 (about 300.5 GW, solar about 164.6 GW), which is over 54% of total installed capacity of about 552 GW.
- India is 3rd in the world in total renewable capacity (after China and USA, IRENA 2026) and 4th in wind.
- Even so, coal still produces about 70–75% of the electricity generated, because coal plants run round the clock while solar works only in daytime.
- Target: 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030.
### 4.4 Coal
| Type | Carbon content | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Anthracite | 80–95% (best) | Hard, burns with little smoke; small amounts in J&K |
| Bituminous | 60–80% | Most common in India; coking coal for steel |
| Lignite (brown coal) | 40–55% | High moisture; Neyveli (Tamil Nadu) |
| Peat | Below 40% | First stage of coal formation |

- Gondwana coal (about 250 million years old) is about 98% of India's reserves – Damodar, Mahanadi, Godavari, Son valleys. Tertiary coal is found in the North-East.
- India is the world's 2nd largest coal producer and consumer. Production crossed 1 billion tonnes in FY 2023-24.
- Coal India Ltd (1975) has its HQ in Kolkata. Most reserves: Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh.
- Raniganj (WB) is the oldest coalfield.
- Clean coal ideas: washeries, supercritical/ultra-supercritical plants, coal gasification (target 100 MT by 2030), FGD, CBM.
### 4.5 Oil, gas and nuclear
- Petroleum: India imports about 85–88% of its crude oil. Digboi (Assam, 1901) is the oldest refinery; Jamnagar (Reliance) is the world's largest refining complex. Mumbai High is the largest offshore field. Strategic Petroleum Reserves: Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru, Padur.
- Natural gas is about 6–7% of India's energy mix; target 15% by 2030. City gas distribution and PNG are expanding. CBM at Raniganj.
- Nuclear power: run by NPCIL. Tarapur (1969) was the first plant; Kudankulam (Tamil Nadu, with Russia) is the largest.
| Stage 1: PHWR using natural uranium | ➜ |
|---|---|

| Stage 2: Fast Breeder Reactors using plutonium (PFBR, Kalpakkam) Stage 3: Thorium-based reactors | ➜ |
|---|---|

Three-stage programme planned by Dr Homi J. Bhabha. India has large thorium reserves in monazite sands (Kerala, Odisha coast). Target: 100 GW nuclear by 2047 (Nuclear Energy Mission, with small modular reactors).

## বাংলা নোট – অধ্যায় ৪: শক্তির উৎস ও ভারতের পরিস্থিতি
- শক্তির ভাগ: নবায়নযোগ্য বনাম অনবায়নযোগ্য; প্রচলিত বনাম অপ্রচলিত; প্রাথমিক বনাম গৌণ (বিদ্যুৎ গৌণ শক্তি);
- বাণিজ্যিক বনাম অ-বাণিজ্যিক।
- একক: ১ kWh = ৩.৬ MJ ≈ ৮৬০ kcal; ১ ক্যালরি = ৪.১৮৬ J; ১ HP = ৭৪৬ W; ১ toe ≈ ১০⁷ kcal। হাইড্রোজেনে প্রতি কেজিতে শক্তি সবচেয়ে বেশি।
- ৩১ মার্চ ২০২৬ (PIB): সৌর ১৫০.২৬ GW, বায়ু ৫৬.০৯ GW, বড় জলবিদ্যুৎ ৫১.৪১ GW, মোট নবায়নযোগ্য ২৭৪.৬৮ GW, পারমাণবিক ৮.৭৮ GW, মোট অ-জীবাশ্ম ২৮৩.৪৬ GW।
- জুলাই ২০২৬-এ অ-জীবাশ্ম ক্ষমতা ৩০০ GW ছাড়িয়েছে (মোটের ৫৪%-এর বেশি)। নবায়নযোগ্য ক্ষমতায় ভারত বিশ্বে তৃতীয়, বায়ুতে চতুর্থ। তবু উৎপাদিত বিদ্যুতের ~৭০–৭৫% আসে কয়লা থেকে।
- কয়লা: অ্যানথ্রাসাইট (৮০–৯৫% কার্বন, শ্রেষ্ঠ), বিটুমিনাস (সবচেয়ে বেশি), লিগনাইট (নেভেলি), পিট। ভারতের ~৯৮% কয়লা গন্ডোয়ানা যুগের। কোল ইন্ডিয়া (১৯৭৫), সদর কলকাতা।
- খনিজ তেল: ~৮৫–৮৮% আমদানি; ডিগবয় প্রাচীনতম শোধনাগার; জামনগর বৃহত্তম। গ্যাসের ভাগ ২০৩০-এ ১৫% করার লক্ষ্য।
- পারমাণবিক: হোমি ভাবার তিন-ধাপ কর্মসূচি (প্রাকৃতিক ইউরেনিয়াম ➜ প্লুটোনিয়াম ➜ থোরিয়াম)। তারাপুর প্রথম, কুদানকুলাম বৃহত্তম। ২০৪৭-এ ১০০ GW লক্ষ্য।
- রাজ্য: DVC (৭ জুলাই ১৯৪৮, প্রথম বহুমুখী নদী প্রকল্প); WBPDCL-এর বক্রেশ্বর, কোলাঘাট, সাগরদিঘি, সাঁওতালডিহি, বান্ডেল; NTPC ফারাক্কা; CESC কলকাতা।
- পুরুলিয়া পাম্পড স্টোরেজ ৯০০ MW (অযোধ্যা পাহাড়); তুর্গা প্রকল্প প্রস্তাবিত। বাজেট ২০২৬-২৭: ২ লক্ষ রুফটপ সোলার, ₹১০০ কোটি।

chapters.title: 5. Energy Conservation, Efficiency & Energy Audit
chapters.notes:
### 5.1 Why conserve energy?
- "Energy saved is energy produced." Saving one unit at the user end saves more than one unit at the power plant, because of transmission losses.
- Benefits: lower bills, less import of oil and gas, energy security, less pollution and CO₂, lower need for new power plants.
- Energy conservation = using less energy (switching off). Energy efficiency = getting the same output with less energy (LED instead of a bulb).
### 5.2 Energy Conservation Act, 2001
- Key facts
- Passed in 2001, came into force on 1 March 2002.
- Set up the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) on 1 March 2002 under the Ministry of Power.
- States act through a State Designated Agency (SDA).
- Designated consumers (energy-intensive industries such as thermal power, steel, cement, aluminium, fertiliser, chlor-alkali, pulp & paper, textiles, refineries, railways, DISCOMs) must appoint a certified energy manager, get a mandatory energy audit by an accredited energy auditor, and meet energy-consumption norms.
**Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2022**
- Allows a carbon credit trading scheme (CCTS notified 2023).
- Designated consumers can be required to use a minimum share of non-fossil energy.
- Building code widened to large residential buildings: the Energy Conservation and Sustainable Building Code (ECSBC).
- Efficiency standards for vehicles and ships; higher penalties.
### 5.3 Main programmes
| Programme | Key facts |
|---|---|
| PAT (Perform, Achieve and Trade) | Launched 2012 under NMEEE. Each designated consumer gets a target for Specific Energy Consumption (SEC). Those who save more get ESCerts (1 ESCert = 1 toe saved) to sell to those who fall short. Now moving into the carbon market (CCTS) |
| Standards & Labelling (Star rating) | Started 2006. 1 to 5 stars; 5 stars = most efficient. Mandatory for ACs, refrigerators, tube lights, distribution transformers, geysers and more. BEE set 24 °C as the default temperature for new ACs (2020) |
| ECBC | Energy Conservation Building Code for commercial buildings, 2007. Eco-Niwas Samhita (2018) for homes. Now ECSBC |
| UJALA | Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All, 5 Jan 2015. Over 36 crore LED bulbs distributed. Run by EESL |
| SLNP | Street Lighting National Programme (2015): LED street lights |
| EESL | Energy Efficiency Services Ltd (2009), a joint venture of NTPC, PFC, REC and POWERGRID. Works as an ESCO (energy service company) |
| Transport | CAFE fuel-efficiency norms for cars, BS-VI (1 April 2020), FAME I & II and PM E- DRIVE (2024) for electric vehicles |
| Grid side | Smart meters (RDSS, 2021), time-of-day tariffs, Demand Side Management (DSM) |
| Awareness | National Energy Conservation Day – 14 December; National Energy Conservation Awards; State Energy Efficiency Index (BEE) |

### 5.4 Energy audit
Definition (EC Act): verification, monitoring and analysis of the use of energy, including a technical report with recommendations to improve energy efficiency, a cost-benefit analysis and an action plan to reduce energy use.
| Type | What it does |
|---|---|
| Preliminary / walk-through audit | Quick look (1–2 days), uses existing bills and data, finds obvious savings and areas for a deeper study |
| Detailed / comprehensive audit | Measures every major system, energy balance, detailed savings and investment proposals |
| Targeted / investment-grade audit | Focus on one system or a big investment decision |

| Pre-audit planning | ➜ Data collection (bills, logs) ➜ Field measurements ➜ |
|---|---|

| Analysis & energy balance Implement & monitor | ➜ Recommendations with payback ➜ Report ➜ |
|---|---|

Audit instruments Power analyser (kW, kVA, power factor, harmonics) · Lux meter (light) · Thermal imaging / IR camera (hot spots, insulation loss) · Flue gas analyser (O₂, CO₂, CO in boiler exhaust) · Ultrasonic flow meter · Tachometer (speed) · Anemometer (air velocity) · Pyrometer / infrared thermometer · Ultrasonic leak detector (compressed air).
**Key terms**
- Specific Energy Consumption (SEC) = energy used ÷ units of product (e.g. GJ per tonne of steel).
- Used for benchmarking.
- Sankey diagram: shows energy flows and losses with arrows whose width is proportional to energy.
- Simple payback period = investment ÷ annual savings. Example: a VFD costs ₹2 lakh and saves ₹1 lakh a year ➜ payback = 2 years.
### 5.5 Energy-saving techniques in industry
**Electrical**
- Power factor correction with capacitor banks: brings PF close to 1, lowers kVA demand, current, losses and penalties.
- Energy-efficient motors: IE1 (standard), IE2 (high), IE3 (premium), IE4 (super premium). Right-size motors; avoid idle running.
- Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs) on pumps and fans. Affinity laws: flow ∝ speed, pressure ∝ speed², power ∝ speed³ . So 20% lower speed saves almost 50% power.
- Lighting: LED (about 100+ lumens/W) vs CFL (about 60) vs incandescent (about 15). Use daylight, sensors, timers.
- Compressed air is the costliest utility: fix leaks, lower pressure, use the right nozzle.
- Control maximum demand; use off-peak hours.
**Thermal**
- Waste heat recovery: economiser (pre-heats boiler feed water with flue gas), air pre-heater / recuperator, waste heat boilers.
- Cogeneration (CHP): makes power and useful heat together; overall efficiency 70–85% versus about 35% for a normal thermal plant. Trigeneration adds cooling.
- Boiler efficiency: control excess air (check O₂ in flue gas), clean heat surfaces, blow-down control, insulate pipes, maintain steam traps, recover condensate.
- Boiler efficiency is checked by the direct method (output ÷ input) or the indirect (heat loss)
- method.
Buildings and homes Star-rated appliances, AC at 24–26 °C, LED lights, solar water heaters, good insulation, cool roofs, natural ventilation, switching off standby loads, pressure cookers, public transport.

- "সঞ্চিত শক্তিই উৎপাদিত শক্তি।" সংরক্ষণ মানে কম ব্যবহার; দক্ষতা মানে একই কাজ কম শক্তিতে।

- PAT (২০১২): লক্ষ্যের বেশি সাশ্রয়ে ESCert (১ ESCert = ১ toe)। স্টার লেবেল (২০০৬): ৫ তারা সবচেয়ে দক্ষ;

- এনার্জি অডিট: প্রাথমিক (walk-through) ও বিস্তারিত। যন্ত্র: পাওয়ার অ্যানালাইজার, লাক্স মিটার, থার্মাল ক্যামেরা, ফ্লুগ্যাস অ্যানালাইজার।
- SEC = শক্তি ÷ উৎপাদন; স্যাঙ্কি চিত্রে শক্তির প্রবাহ ও অপচয় দেখানো হয়; পেব্যাক = বিনিয়োগ ÷ বার্ষিক সাশ্রয়।
- কৌশল: ক্যাপাসিটর দিয়ে পাওয়ার ফ্যাক্টর উন্নতি; IE3/IE4 মোটর; VFD — শক্তি গতির ঘনফলের সমানুপাতিক, তাই ২০% গতি কমালে প্রায় ৫০% সাশ্রয়; LED; সংকুচিত বাতাসের লিক বন্ধ।
- তাপীয়: ইকোনোমাইজার, এয়ার প্রি-হিটার, কোজেনারেশন (৭০–৮৫% দক্ষতা), অতিরিক্ত বাতাস নিয়ন্ত্রণ, ইনসুলেশন, স্টিম ট্র্যাপ, কনডেনসেট পুনরুদ্ধার।

chapters.title: 6. Renewable Energy: Solar, Wind, Hydro, Bio, Hydrogen & Storage
chapters.notes:
### 6.1 Institutions
| Body | Facts |
|---|---|
| MNRE | Started as DNES (1982) ➜ Ministry of Non-Conventional Energy Sources (1992) ➜ renamed MNRE in 2006 |
| IREDA | Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency, 1987; finances RE projects |
| SECI | Solar Energy Corporation of India, 2011; runs RE auctions |
| Research institutes | NISE Gurugram (solar), NIWE Chennai (wind), NIBE Kapurthala (bio-energy) |
| International | IRENA (2009, HQ Abu Dhabi), ISA (2015, HQ Gurugram), Global Biofuels Alliance (launched at G20 New Delhi, Sep 2023) |
| West Bengal | WBREDA (West Bengal Renewable Energy Development Agency) and WB Green Energy Development Corporation (WBGEDCL) |

### 6.2 Solar energy
- India gets about 4–7 kWh/m²/day of sunlight, with about 300 sunny days a year. NISE estimates solar potential at about 748 GW (ground-mounted).
- Solar PV converts sunlight directly into electricity by the photovoltaic effect (discovered by Becquerel, 1839). Material: mainly silicon (mono-crystalline is most efficient, poly-crystalline, thin-film). Commercial module efficiency is about 20–22%. Panels give DC; an inverter changes it to AC.
- Solar thermal: solar water heaters, solar cookers, dryers, Concentrated Solar Power (CSP)
- using mirrors.
- Types: grid-connected ground plants, rooftop, floating solar (on reservoirs), canal-top, agri-voltaics, off-grid mini-grids.
- Leading states: Rajasthan (1st), Gujarat, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra.
| Solar park / first | Fact |
|---|---|
| Bhadla (Jodhpur, Rajasthan) | About 2,245 MW, one of the world's largest solar parks |
| Pavagada (Karnataka) | About 2,050 MW |
| Khavda (Kutch, Gujarat) | About 30 GW hybrid RE park, the world's largest under construction |
| Cochin Airport | World's first fully solar-powered airport (2015) |
| Modhera (Gujarat) | India's first solar-powered village (2022) |

| Scheme | Key facts |
|---|---|
| JNNSM (National Solar Mission) | 2010; target raised from 20 GW to 100 GW by 2022 |
| PM-KUSUM | 2019; solar pumps and small solar plants for farmers (Components A, B, C) |
| PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana | Feb 2024; rooftop solar for 1 crore households, up to 300 units free a month; outlay about ₹75,000 crore. WB 2026-27 budget targets 2 lakh systems |
| PLI for solar modules · ALMM | Promote domestic high-efficiency module manufacturing |

### 6.3 Wind energy
- Power in wind ∝ air density × swept area × (wind speed)³. So doubling wind speed gives 8 times the power.
- Betz limit: a turbine can capture at most 59.3% (16/27) of wind energy.
- Cut-in speed about 3–4 m/s; cut-out speed (storm) about 25 m/s. Types: Horizontal Axis (HAWT) – common; Vertical Axis (VAWT).
- Potential about 1,164 GW at 150 m hub height (NIWE). Leading states: Gujarat, Tamil Nadu (Muppandal – one of the largest wind farms), Karnataka, Maharashtra, Rajasthan.
- Offshore wind: target 30 GW by 2030, mainly off Gujarat and Tamil Nadu. Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy 2018.
### 6.4 Hydro energy
| Class (India) | Capacity |
|---|---|
| Micro hydro | Up to 100 kW |
| Mini hydro | 101 kW – 2 MW |
| Small hydro (under MNRE) | Up to 25 MW |
| Large hydro (under Ministry of Power) | Above 25 MW; declared renewable in 2019 |

Pumped Storage Plants (PSP) pump water uphill using surplus (solar) power and generate at peak time – a giant "water battery". Example: Purulia PSP, 900 MW (WB).
### 6.5 Bio-energy
- Biomass: wood, crop residue, bagasse (sugar mill cogeneration), municipal waste-to-energy.
- Biogas: anaerobic digestion of cow dung and organic waste. Contains methane 50–70% and CO₂ 30–40%. The slurry is good manure.
- GOBARdhan (2018): waste to biogas in villages. SATAT (Oct 2018): Compressed Biogas (CBG)
- plants.
- Ethanol blending: India reached E20 (20% ethanol in petrol) in 2025 , five years before the old 2030 target. 2G ethanol is made from crop residue (Panipat 2G refinery, 2022). National Policy on Biofuels 2018 (amended 2022).
- Biodiesel from non-edible oils (Jatropha, used cooking oil). Sustainable Aviation Fuel: 1% blending target for international flights by 2027.
### 6.6 Geothermal and ocean energy
| Type | Facts |
|---|---|
| Geothermal | Heat from inside the Earth. Sites: Puga Valley (Ladakh, ONGC pilot), Tattapani (Chhattisgarh), Manikaran (HP). In WB: hot springs at Bakreshwar (Birbhum) |
| Tidal | Uses the rise and fall of tides. Best sites: Gulf of Khambhat and Gulf of Kutch (Gujarat), Sundarbans (a 3.75 MW project at Durgaduani creek was planned but dropped) |
| Wave | Pilot at Vizhinjam (Kerala) |
| OTEC | Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion – needs a temperature difference of about 20 °C between warm surface water and cold deep water. NIOT plant for desalination at Kavaratti (Lakshadweep) |

### 6.7 Green hydrogen
| Colour | How it is made |
|---|---|
| Grey | From natural gas (steam methane reforming), CO₂ released |
| Blue | Same, but CO₂ captured and stored (CCS) |
| Green | Electrolysis of water using renewable power – no CO₂ |
| Brown / black | From coal gasification |

- National Green Hydrogen Mission
- Approved 4 January 2023; outlay ₹19,744 crore.
- Target: 5 million tonnes (MMT) green hydrogen a year by 2030, with about 125 GW of linked RE.
- SIGHT programme: incentives for electrolyser manufacturing and green hydrogen production.
- Uses: refineries, fertiliser (green ammonia), steel, shipping, heavy transport.
Fuel cell: hydrogen + oxygen ➜ electricity + water + heat (no burning, no pollution at use).
### 6.8 Energy storage and grid integration
- Solar and wind are intermittent (variable). Solutions: battery energy storage systems (BESS), mostly lithium-ion (with a Viability Gap Funding scheme), pumped hydro, green hydrogen.
- Green Energy Corridors: new transmission lines to carry RE from RE-rich states. Duck curve:
- midday solar surplus followed by an evening peak.
- Waiver of inter-state transmission (ISTS) charges, Renewable Purchase Obligations (now Renewable Consumption Obligations) for DISCOMs and big users.
| Advantages of RE ➜ Never runs out ➜ No fuel cost, cheaper now (solar tariffs near ₹2.5/kWh) ➜ Low emissions ➜ Energy security, less import ➜ Rural jobs and electrification | Challenges ➜ Intermittent, needs storage ➜ Large land needs ➜ Grid stability ➜ Import of cells and lithium ➜ Waste from old panels and batteries |
|---|---|

West Bengal angle: its RE share is still low compared with RE-rich states. Key points are rooftop solar (2 lakh target in Budget 2026-27), the open-access policy, solar mini-grids in the Sundarban islands (Sagar Island was a pioneer), Purulia pumped storage, hydro in North Bengal, biogas, and geothermal at Bakreshwar.
## বাংলা নোট – অধ্যায় ৬: নবায়নযোগ্য শক্তি
- MNRE (২০০৬-এ নাম), IREDA ১৯৮৭, SECI ২০১১; NISE গুরুগ্রাম, NIWE চেন্নাই; IRENA (আবুধাবি), ISA (গুরুগ্রাম)। রাজ্যে WBREDA।
- সৌর: দিনে প্রতি বর্গমিটারে ৪–৭ kWh; বছরে ~৩০০ রৌদ্রোজ্জ্বল দিন। ফটোভোল্টাইক প্রভাব; সিলিকন সেল; দক্ষতা ~২০–২২%; ইনভার্টার DC থেকে AC করে। শীর্ষ রাজ্য রাজস্থান; ভাদলা, পাভাগড়া, খাভড়া (৩০ GW)।
- প্রকল্প: জাতীয় সৌর মিশন ২০১০; PM-KUSUM ২০১৯ (কৃষকদের সোলার পাম্প); PM সূর্য ঘর মুফত বিজলি যোজনা (ফেব্রুয়ারি ২০২৪, ১ কোটি বাড়ি, মাসে ৩০০ ইউনিট বিনামূল্যে)।
- বায়ু: শক্তি বাতাসের গতির ঘনফলের সমানুপাতিক (গতি দ্বিগুণ হলে শক্তি ৮ গুণ); বেটজ সীমা ৫৯.৩%; শীর্ষে গুজরাট ও তামিলনাড়ু (মুপ্পান্ডাল); ২০৩০-এ ৩০ GW অফশোর লক্ষ্য।
- ছোট জলবিদ্যুৎ ২৫ MW পর্যন্ত; বড় জলবিদ্যুৎ ২০১৯ থেকে নবায়নযোগ্য। পাম্পড স্টোরেজ = "জলের ব্যাটারি"
- (পুরুলিয়া ৯০০ MW)।
- জৈব শক্তি: বায়োগ্যাসে মিথেন ৫০–৭০%; গোবর-ধন ২০১৮; SATAT ২০১৮ (CBG); ২০২৫-এ E20 (পেট্রোলে ২০% ইথানল) অর্জিত; পানিপথে 2G ইথানল।
- ভূতাপীয়: পুগা ভ্যালি (লাদাখ), রাজ্যে বক্রেশ্বর উষ্ণ প্রস্রবণ। জোয়ার-ভাটা: কচ্ছ ও খাম্বাত উপসাগর, সুন্দরবন (দুর্গাদুয়ানি প্রকল্প পরিত্যক্ত)। OTEC-এ ~২০°C তাপমাত্রা পার্থক্য লাগে।
- সবুজ হাইড্রোজেন: নবায়নযোগ্য বিদ্যুতে জলের তড়িৎ-বিশ্লেষণ। জাতীয় গ্রিন হাইড্রোজেন মিশন ৪ জানুয়ারি ২০২৩, ₹১৯,৭৪৪ কোটি, ২০৩০-এ বছরে ৫ মিলিয়ন টন লক্ষ্য; SIGHT প্রকল্প।
- সঞ্চয়: লিথিয়াম-আয়ন ব্যাটারি (BESS), পাম্পড স্টোরেজ; গ্রিন এনার্জি করিডর। সমস্যা: অনিয়মিত সরবরাহ, জমি, গ্রিডের স্থিতিশীলতা।
